questions.q:
Which of the following interchanges of signs and numbers would make the given equation correct?

25 - 10 ÷ 5 + 15 × 30 = 55
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

Option 1) : × and +, 30 and 25

Given equation is : 25 - 10 ÷ 5 + 15 × 30 = 55

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 30 - 10 ÷ 5 × 15 + 25 = 55

⇒ 30 - 10 ÷ 5 × 15 + 25 = 55

⇒ 30 - 2 × 15 + 25 = 55

⇒ 30 - 30 + 25 = 55

⇒ 55 - 30 = 55

⇒ 25 ≠ 55

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : ÷ and +, 15 and 10

Given equation is : 25 - 10 ÷ 5 + 15 × 30 = 55

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 25 - 15 + 5 ÷ 10 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 - 15 + 5 ÷ 10 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 - 15 + 0.5 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 - 15 + 15 = 55

⇒ 40 - 15 = 55

⇒ 25 ≠ 55

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : × and -, 15 and 10

Given equation is : 25 - 10 ÷ 5 + 15 × 30 = 55

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 25 × 15 ÷ 5 + 10 - 30 = 55

⇒ 25 × 15 ÷ 5 + 10 - 30 = 55

⇒ 25 × 3 + 10 - 30 = 55

⇒ 75 + 10 - 30 = 55

⇒ 85 - 30 = 55

⇒ 55 = 55

LHS = RHS

Option 4) : + and -, 5 and 10

Given equation is : 25 - 10 ÷ 5 + 15 × 30 = 55

After interchanging the two numbers and two signs the equation is as follows : 25 + 5 ÷ 10 - 15 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 + 5 ÷ 10 - 15 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 + 0.5 - 15 × 30 = 55

⇒ 25 + 0.5 - 450 = 55

⇒ 25.5 - 450 = 55

⇒ -424.5 ≠ 55

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "× and -, 15 and 10".

questions.q: Why is PC Mahalanobis' name talked about in the context of Five-Year Plans?
options: He was the chairman of the Planning Commission.
He established the Institute of Economic Growth.
He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.
He was the finance minister during the First Five-Year Plan period.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is He conceptualised the framework for the Second Five-Year Plan.

Key Points

• Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis was an Indian statistician who played a significant role in formulating India's strategy for industrialization in the Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61).

• The Plan, influenced by the Mahalanobis model, stressed the importance of boosting the public sector's role in the economy and targeted significant growth in sectors like steel, electricity, and heavy machinery.

• Although Mahalanobis was not the chairman of the Planning Commission nor the Finance Ministry during this time, his contributions were instrumental for the execution of the economic strategy during the Plan period.

• Therefore, his name is often mentioned alongside the development of these five-year plans in India.

Additional Information Second Five year plan:

• The Second Five-Year Plan, also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, was proposed by Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis in 1955. It was in effect from 1956 to 1961.

• This plan focused on the development of the public sector and aimed to create a socialistic pattern of society.

• This Plan set the precedence for a predominant role of the state which would determine the direction of the economy.

• A substantial part of the plan was focused on increasing industrialization, with a particular emphasis on the development of heavy industries such as steel, heavy engineering, machine making, etc.

• The Plan aimed at a 25% increase in the national income over a period of five years and a transformation in the pattern of industrial production.

• However, the Plan was only partially successful in achieving its objectives, and the target growth rate of national income (5%) was not achieved. Still, it set a clear path for future industrial policies in India.

questions.q: Which autonomous body was operationalised under the Ministry of Surface Transport in 1995?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).

Key Points

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India.

• Operationalised in 1995, the NHAI is responsible for the management of a network of over 70,000 km of national highways in the country.

• It was given the mandate for the development, maintenance, and management of National Highways, which are the arterial roads of the country, designed for high-speed traffic.

• The NHAI is involved in the planning and implementation of various projects like the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), which encompasses the Golden Quadrilateral and the North-South and East-West Corridors.

• It carries out highway projects through a model of public private partnership (PPP) in addition to receiving budgetary support from the central government.

Additional Information

• Border Roads Organization (BRO):

• The BRO is tasked with maintaining road networks in India's border areas and friendly neighbouring countries.

• It works under the Ministry of Defence and plays a crucial role in the strategic and tactical movement of the armed forces.

• Centre for Railway Information System (CRIS):

• CRIS is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Railways.

• It develops and manages the critical Information Technology applications of the Indian Railways.

• Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI):

• IWAI is the statutory authority in charge of the waterways in India for the purpose of shipping and navigation.

• Its tasks include the development and regulation of inland waterways for shipping and navigation.

• It operates under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

questions.q: Micro credit or micro finance is a novel approach to bank with poor. In this approach bank credit is extended to the poor through _.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is self-help groups.

Key Points

• Microfinance or microcredit refers to the provision of financial services, including loans, savings, insurance, and training to people living in poverty.

• These services are typically targeted at underserved populations who do not have access to typical banking services. The approach is designed to support entrepreneurship, empower poor individuals, and stimulate economic growth.

• In this mode of operation, bank credit is extended to the poor through Self Help Groups (SHGs), which are small voluntary associations of poor people created for the purpose of solving their common problems.

• SHGs usually consist of 10-20 individuals from a homogeneous class who come together to pool their resources to cope with emergencies, provide collateral-free loans to members, and often serve as a conduit for formal banking services.

• This approach has proven successful in reaching large numbers of poor individuals, particularly women, and allowing them to partake in income-generating activities.

questions.q: Which state ranks first with a total length of 31.2 thousand km of rivers and canals, which is about 17% of the total length of rivers and canals in the country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

Key Points

• Uttar Pradesh ranks first in the country with a total length of 31.2 thousand kilometers of Rivers and Canals. This constitutes about 17% of the total length of rivers and canals in India.

• The state is drained by two major rivers, the Ganges and the Yamuna, as well as a number of their significant tributaries such as the Ghaghara, Gomti, Chambal, Betwa, and Ken.

• Canals form an integral part of Uttar Pradesh's irrigation system. The Upper Ganges Canal, one of the oldest canals in India, and the Lower Ganges Canal are the lifeblood of swathes of agricultural land in the state.

• These rivers and canals play a critical role in supporting agriculture, which is the mainstay of the state's economy, providing necessary water for farming.

• The extensive network of rivers and canals also supports fisheries and local commerce, and holds cultural and religious significance, with towns like Varanasi and Allahabad being significant religious hubs due to their location on the banks of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers respectively.

• However, water management remains a significant challenge, with issues of drought in some areas and floods in others due to variable rainfall and limited storage capacity.

questions.q: Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was incorporated in the year _.

• HCL's mines and plants are spread across four operating units, namely: Khetri Copper Complex in Rajasthan, Indian Copper Complex in Jharkhand, Malanjkhand Copper Project in Madhya Pradesh, and Taloja Copper Project in Maharashtra.

• It is also responsible for contributing to the supply of copper products, like copper cathodes, continuous cast copper rods, and other by products, such as gold, silver, and sulphuric acid, to the Indian market.

• In the recent years, HCL has been focusing on increasing its production capacity and upgrading its older mines and plants, demonstrating its commitment to the development of the nation's copper industry.

• As a leading copper manufacturer in the country, HCL plays a significant role in India's metal industry, influencing the country's industrial growth and contributing significantly to the nation's economy.

questions.q: Which pioneer scientist used radio waves to transmit signals over distances of several kilometres in the 1890s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Guglielmo Marconi.

Key Points

• Guglielmo Marconi was an Italian inventor and electrical engineer.

• He conducted pioneering work in long-distance radio transmission.

• Marconi developed a practical radio wave-based wireless telegraph system in the late 19th century.

• His system was able to transmit signals over distances of several kilometers.

• Marconi's contributions helped significantly expand the field of telecommunications.

• His work was recognized internationally when he was awarded the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1909.​

Additional Information

• Michael Faraday:

• Michael Faraday was a British scientist who contributed significantly to the field of electromagnetism and electrochemistry.

• He discovered electromagnetic induction, diamagnetism, and the laws of electrolysis.

• Although Faraday discovered electromagnetic fields, he did not work on radio wave transmission.

• Paul Langevin:

• Paul Langevin was a French physicist.

• He is known for his work in developing Langevin dynamics and the Langevin equation.

• He developed the use of ultrasound using piezoelectricity but wasn't involved in radio wave transmission.

• Pierre Weiss:

• Pierre Weiss was a French physicist known for his work in magnetism.

• He introduced the concept of magnetic domains, which helps explain the magnetic behavior in ferromagnetic materials.

• His main work was on magnetism, not on radio wave transmission.

• It functioned as a hostel for Indian students studying in England.

questions.q: Which of the following committees recommended for the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Swaran Singh Committee.

Key Points

• The Swaran Singh Committee was established in 1976 under the leadership of Sardar Swaran Singh, an Indian Politician.

• The committee was specifically constituted to study and suggest changes to the Constitution in relation to the concept of fundamental duties. It was the Swaran Singh Committee that suggested adding a new part outlining citizen duties.

• As a result of this committee's recommendations, the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution in 1976 included the new Part IVA, which specified the fundamental duties of Indian citizens. It comprises Article 51A from (a) to (k).

• The fundamental duties include tenets like respect for the national flag, the constitution, and institutions, promoting brotherhood, protecting the environment, and upholding scientific temper among others.

• The primary aim behind the inclusion of the Fundamental Duties by this committee was to create a balance of rights and duties in the constitution, obliging citizens to act responsibly and assist in maintaining the spirit of democracy in India.

Additional Information

• Sarkaria Commission:

• The Sarkaria Commission was established in 1983 by the central government of India.

• The Commission was set up to examine the relationship and balance of power between state and central governments in the country and suggest changes within the framework of the Constitution.

• It made 247 recommendations to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, and balance between the various levels of government in India.

• The report of the Sarkaria Commission is the first and the most comprehensive attempt to review Centre-State relationship.

• Rajamannar Committee:

• The Rajamannar Committee was constituted by the government of Tamil Nadu in 1969.

• Its task was to examine the entire question concerning state autonomy and the Centre-State relations.

• The committee recommended a drastic overhaul of India’s federal system, with suggestions for the constitution to emerge as a truly federal one rather than quasi-federal.

• The need for such changes arose because of the contention that centralization of power diminishes the effectiveness of regional governments.

• Balwant Rai Mehta Committee:

• The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee was a committee appointed by the Government of India in 1957.

• The aim of this Committee was to examine the working of the Community Development Programme (1952) and the National Extension Service (1953) and to suggest measures for their better working.

• Significantly, their recommendations led to the birth of Panchayati Raj Institutions in India, outlining a three-tier system, including village, block, and district levels.

• The report of the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee is considered a landmark in the evolution of local self-government (Panchayati Raj) institutions in India.

∴ The correct answer is 560.
